description: Refusal codes of the planner (spec/plan.md, spec/run-config.md §8, D79). A refusal reports its code, a JSON pointer into the run config (or a model location) and a message; conformance tests compare the code and the pointer only. 'rule' is the rule number of spec/run-config.md §8, or null for a refusal that section does not list.

codes.meaning: The run config does not validate against its JSON Schema (pointer "", the document root), or a duration read from a parameter is not a positive finite number (pointer: the duration's key).
The run config's esm_integrator version is not one this planner implements.
The model is toy:<problem>, which only the conformance harness accepts.

The model does not load or validate with EarthSciAST; the message carries EarthSciAST's own code. A rejected solver.time_span whose cause is a rule-14 one takes that code instead (spec/plan.md §4 step 3).
The model's solver.external does not resolve to this run config.
EarthSciAST refused to flatten the model or expand its references.
The flattened model has algebraic unknowns; algebraic operators need U6 (M4b).
The flattened model has continuous or discrete events; condition and map operators need U6 (M4b).
A parameter carries an update rule; none is planned at M2, schedule and data included.
The flattened model reads data-loader fields; forcing epochs arrive at M3.
An index set is not an interval with an integer size.
A map operator or map node; map operators need U6 (M4b).
An observed step limit in step.limits or subcycle.limits; limit operators need U6 (M4b).
A solve node; algebraic operators need U6 (M4b).
A coupled node with algebraic operators (D3b, after M6).
A split_explicit node (M7).
A crossing parameter-update rule (not in v1). Reported whenever any parameter has one, whatever the parameter order: it wins over unsupported_parameter_update.
axes names an index set that does not exist or names one twice, or more than two horizontal axes result.
A qualified name does not resolve in the flattened model, or a precision key names no operator, node or default (spec/plan.md §7.1).
A qualified name resolves to the wrong kind of variable.
The schedule names an operator that is neither defined nor an existing default operator.
A term is matched by two operators' selectors.
An operator's selector matches no term. With several, the first in code-point order is reported.
A term that reads variables of two or more other components is matched by no selector while some selector uses components.
A contribution has an empty origins list.
An operator, named or default, is advanced by no node of the schedule (a frozen entry counts as advancing). Pointer: /operators/<op>, or /schedule for a default operator.
An operator is named by two leaf or coupled nodes (a strang running a child twice is one place; frozen entries do not count).
An imex partition leaves an operator of the leaf in neither part or puts one in both, or an IMEXEuler leaf has no imex.
Two nodes have the same id, or a given id equals a path the planner assigns.
A path-form node id on a node whose path it is not.
An every node with hold: tendency whose child is not a single leaf.
A tstop that is not t0 plus a multiple of a fixed step.dt, under a root that cannot land on it.
A state or rhs precision role contradicts a declared element_type, or a leaf's written states declare different element_types. Pointer: the precision entry that set the role, /precision/<key>.
The rhs role is below the state role. Pointer: the precision entry that set the role, /precision/<key>.
Precision entries for two operators of one leaf disagree on a role. Pointer: the second entry in the leaf's operator order, /precision/<key>.

A jacobian or factors role below rhs on a Rosenbrock method other than Rosenbrock23; for an alg of "auto", checked once spec/plan.md §5.5.3 resolves the method. Pointer: the precision entry that set the role, /precision/<key>.
An adjoint.wrt entry matches nothing; at M2 every forcing: entry does (spec/plan.md §7.6).
An adjoint.wrt entry names a parameter bound by bind_dt.
step has neither dt nor limits and the schedule root is not a single adaptive leaf or coupled node.
A leaf with dt omitted whose method has no embedded error estimate.
No source gives a run interval. Pointer: /time; a refusal about the caller's interval is at "".
The interval's end is not after its start. Pointer: /time, "" for the caller's interval, /model for the model's solver.time_span.
A timestamp names a day its month does not have. Pointer: the timestamp's key, "" for the caller's, /model for the model's solver.time_span.
A timestamp is given and the model's time-origin field cannot be read. Pointer: the timestamp's key ("" for the caller's, /model for solver.time_span).
An adaptive leaf binds a parameter to the leaf step but gives no control.dt0. Pointer: the binding, the leaf's bind_dt or /operators/<op>/bind_dt.
An output or saveat time lies outside the run interval. Cannot occur at M2: saveat is a duration whose multiples are taken inside (t0, tf] (D83).

An auto choice has no M2 resolution: a stiff global leaf, a stiff pointwise leaf whose Jacobian storage is not block_diagonal, a stencil leaf with a stiff column operator and no dt, or an implicit method on a stencil or global leaf with linsolve omitted.
EarthSciASTDiff refused to differentiate a term or an operator. Pointer: /model.
No declared shape of a non-lifted variable has a lifted state's extents. Pointer: /model.
The model has a top-level component named _jacobian. Pointer: /model.
ranks or tiles divide a horizontal axis the model does not have. Pointer: /partition.
ranks times tiles exceeds an axis's size.
partition.shards entries for two operators of one leaf disagree.
The operators' right-hand sides do not sum to the model's.
An operator's band Jacobian disagrees with the independent Jacobian.
An operator has no term, or no band although a term reads a state.
